title: Percent of a Number: Mental Math + Markup/Discount Shortcut
preview: Build percent fluency from 10% upward, into >100% and the markup/discount shortcut. This is the *first* of several 7.RP.2 strands — tax/tip, percent change, and proportions are separate slices.

body.goal: Students build mental fluency with percent of a number — composing percents from 10%, computing percents over 100%, and discovering the one-step shortcut for markup and discount (e.g., 80% of $80 instead of subtracting 20%).
body.launch: Run the percent-to-decimal warm-up. Then start the slice. The diamond is step 13 — let groups fight over which method is faster (and why both work).
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up by converting common percents to decimals.

steps.teacherNote: Half of 10%. Composition starts to pay off.
Diamond: 100% IS the number. Anchor for steps 12-14.
Diamond: more than 100% means BIGGER than the original. 200% = double.
Diamond: two methods. (a) 20% of 80 = 16, then 80 - 16 = 64. (b) 80% of 80 = 64 in one step. Push: which is faster?

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Diamond: NOT the same as enrichment 3. 10/60 ≈ 16.7%. Going up 20% and back down isn't the same magnitude.

body.consolidation: Pull it together. 'On step 13, what's the fastest way? Some groups did 20% then subtracted. Some did 80% directly. Which is faster? Why does it work?' (Because 100% - 20% = 80% — they're computing the part that *remains*.) 'In enrichment 3 vs 4, going up 20% and back down 20% didn't return to the start. Why?' (Because the *base* changed — the 20% off the new bigger number is bigger than 20% of the original.)
